players.product: two Project Suncatcher TPU prototype satellites for Google and Pelican satellites integrating NVIDIA IGX Thor on-orbit compute

quarterly_data.signal: Planet Q2 FY2027 results: record revenue of $116 million, approximately 58% year-over-year growth; non-GAAP gross margin 59% vs 61% a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA profit $13.9 million. CFO: the outperformance came mainly from satellite services, specifically the handover of the first Pelican for the Swedish Armed Forces (point-in-time revenue).

Planet revenue mix: CFO: defense and intelligence revenue grew more than 90% year-on-year (including satellite services), commercial more than 15%, civil government over 5%; by region approximately 3% in Latin America, over 15% in Asia Pacific, approximately 25% in North America and over 130% in EMEA; point-in-time revenue was 12% of revenue vs 1% a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 90%; more than 15%; over 5%; over 130%; 12%

quarterly_data.signal: Planet ACV metrics (exclude satellite services): recurring ACV 98% of end-of-period ACV book of business; approximately 94% annual or multi-year contracts; net dollar retention 109%, 110% with win backs.

Planet backlog: CFO: remaining performance obligations approximately $753 million, up approximately 9% year-over-year (46% within 12 months, 68% within 24 months); backlog including termination-for-convenience contracts approximately $815 million, up approximately 11% (50% within 12 months, 70% within 24 months), implying that by executing on contracts already in backlog Planet could recognize over $400 million in revenue over the next four quarters, not including new business or renewals.

Planet FY2027 guidance (low end raised): revenue $430 million to $441 million (40% to 43% growth); non-GAAP gross margin 55% to 57%; adjusted EBITDA $3 million to $10 million; capex approximately $100 million-$115 million; managing to be adjusted free cash flow positive for the year and aiming for Rule of 40.
quarterly_data.figure: $430 million and $441 million; 40% to 43%; $3 million and $10 million; $100 million-$115 million

quarterly_data.signal: Planet Q3 FY2027 outlook: revenue $101 million to $105 million (approximately 27% year-on-year growth at the midpoint); non-GAAP gross margin 56% to 58%; adjusted EBITDA loss of $6 million to $1 million; capex approximately $30 million-$37 million. CFO: Q2 outperformance partly shifted revenue from Q3 (timing of the satellite handover) without changing the full-year outlook.

Planet capex: CFO: Q2 capex including capitalized software approximately $29 million, just above guidance due to timing of Pelican procurements and AI software development; capex to increase in future quarters to scale manufacturing in San Francisco and Berlin, invest in supply chain resiliency and build next-generation fleets - advance procurements of long-lead items for Pelican and Owl.

Planet satellite services pipeline: CEO: over $4 billion of identified satellite services opportunities, over 25% (about $1 billion) qualified as near-term pipeline (near term meaning quarters, not years), spread across EMEA, APAC and North America and now extending from defense into civil government, though still mainly defense and intelligence deals; Planet delivered a first satellite in orbit within two and four months of contract award for its two most recent satellite services partnerships.

Planet NGA contract (August, after the quarter): new $8 million contract with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency to deploy Planet's Global Monitoring Service (GMS) in support of national defense priorities, with options to expand and extend; CEO: Planet was the only vendor considered; the program grew out of a Defense Innovation Unit pilot in support of INDOPACOM.

Planet German government tender (August): Planet was awarded a tender for dedicated capacity satellite services with options and a maximum possible value of EUR 25 million over five years - Planet's first satellite services deal for a federal civil government agency.

Planet Swedish Armed Forces: the first satellite for the Swedish Armed Forces launched in May, four months after the satellite services contract was signed; Planet completed commissioning and handed over this first sovereign Earth observation satellite in Q2, contributing to the revenue outperformance.

Planet data-center monitoring: Planet signed a six-figure expanded renewal with a hyperscaler AI developer for global monitoring of data centers and semiconductor manufacturing facility construction using Pelican high-resolution data (CEO: Planet's first win with an AI hyperscaler for data center monitoring); CFO: interest in data center monitoring across insurance, energy and financial services.

Planet other deals: a seven-figure one-year agreement with a European defense and intelligence customer for high-resolution global mosaics; a new contract with the Rwanda Space Agency for national high-resolution data and analytics (Planet's first national program of its kind in Africa); a renewal with the New Mexico State Land Office (partnership since 2019, monitoring over 9 million acres); partnerships with FarmQA (AI agronomic tools) and Bragger Technologies (spatial intelligence platform).

Planet maritime domain awareness: CEO: Planet's U.S. Navy partnership alone images 13 million square kilometers of ocean territory; the Navy work was sole-sourced on its second award; Planet is the only company doing a daily scan.

Planet Tanager and SuperDoves: Planet shipped its second Tanager hyperspectral satellite and 18 SuperDoves to the launch site, slated for launch this fall aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission; the second Tanager doubles capacity for methane and CO2 detections for partner Carbon Mapper.

Planet next-generation Pelican tech demo: launched in July with advancements across payload, on-orbit compute and satellite-to-satellite communications, on the path to 30-cm class resolution imagery; not expected to serve customers. CEO: it has RF (not optical) inter-satellite links; optical crosslinks come in later missions, developed in-house together with the main telescope system for an independent supply chain.

Planet Owl: next-generation monitoring satellite upgrading data from 3-m to 1-m class resolution and cutting latency to as little as an hour in key areas, delivering roughly 10 times more data about 10 times faster, with onboard AI detection and satellite-to-satellite communication; Planet is beginning to accelerate the program. CEO: a definite price increase opportunity; customers expect prices to go up.

Planet manufacturing capacity: the new German satellite manufacturing facility is expected to roughly double Planet's manufacturing capacity, with clean room fit-out scheduled for September and building to begin in the facility this year; under a launch partnership announced in July, Isar Aerospace is scheduled to launch a Pelican next year that Planet plans to build in the new German facility.

Planet launch and supply chain: CEO: strong demand for SpaceX rideshare missions; launch prices, about $20,000 a kilogram when Planet started, are now significantly less but have been going up a little; Planet has launched 688 Earth-imaging satellites on 42 rockets of 10 different varieties (SpaceX 16 times, the Indian PSLV seven times) and is investing to secure launch access and diversify; Planet has stockpiled critical components. CFO: advance procurement of longer lead time items is part of the raised capex.

Planet AI: CEO: the AI app (natural-language queries of Planet's 10-year daily archive, model-agnostic) has progressed to open beta; Planet believes it has under 5% market share of the Earth observation market excluding satellite services and that AI is expanding the market to users without geospatial expertise.

Planet long-term targets: CFO: the business can deliver adjusted EBITDA profitability of 25%+ with healthy free cash flow; gross margin target amended to north of 60%, depending on the mix of business.

Planet cash flow: CFO: year to date approximately $68 million net cash from operating activities, free cash flow $21 million and adjusted free cash flow $29 million (excluding non-recurring litigation settlement payments).

Planet U.S. government demand: CEO: the administration is leaning into commercial solutions, with meaningful expansion of commercial-type operational budgets across NGA, NRO and the department; substantial programs are targeted in the government's FY2027, which has not yet passed Congress.
